evidence_note: IPDB 3657 Notes: 'First use of the Mystic Lines feature.' cdyn beauty_beach: 'First appearing on Border Beauty'. Catalog holds border-beauty (Bally, 1965) but it has no mystic-lines attachment; catalog's earliest mystic-lines carrier is beauty-beach (1965), which is wrong by source.

The Bally Hole is playfield hole #16, one of the 25 trap holes on a bingo playfield (IPDB 382 features: 'Trap holes (25), Magic Squares, Bally Hole'). bally-hole currently has no parent in the feature DAG; it should sit under trap-holes.

cdyn Game Features defines 'next game award' as a feature family from the one-ball games — something done this game enables a feature on the next ('Are you going to play again?...of course!') — grouping ballyhole, red letter game, ok game, futurity game, sunny circles. No catalog record; the bally-hole description names the concept in bare prose.

cdyn treats in-line scoring and section scoring as the two bingo win systems ('section scoring determined winners by balls being in the same colored pattern on the card, and most importantly, the numbers did not need to be adjacent to win'). No catalog records; the bingo-cards, magic-screen and mystic-lines descriptions each gloss them in bare prose. Candidates for feature vocabulary.

No generic backglass feature record exists; the vocabulary holds only the variants mirrored-backglasses and lenticular-backglasses, which would parent under it. The bingo-cards description has to gloss the term in bare prose ('the upright glass panel in the machine's head'). A universal-part record on the pattern of balls/speakers/knockers.

cdyn Game Features: 'roto feature — United's answer to Bally's magic squares, the eight numbers forming a square around the center number of the 5x5 main card could be rotated around.' No catalog gameplay-feature covers this; distinct from roto-targets (flipper-game mechanism). Would need research into which United bingos carry it.
